Hi Erin — thanks for the clear summary. High level response and proposed next steps below.

Quick mapping (short):
- H100: pick for the 32k long-context model when memory for KV + activations is the limiter. Best for highest throughput on long prefix reuse with heavy quantized 8-bit int8 flows. Rationale: headroom for large kv cache & faster fp16 kernels for attention-heavy batches.
- A100: pick as the balanced workhorse for mixed workloads when memory and steady throughput both matter. Good reserve SKU where you want predictable throughput but don't need H100-level memory bandwidth.
- L4: pick for low-cost, low-latency short-context chat at high concurrency. Great for small models and large-scale scale-out. Not suitable if your long-context model exceeds ~48GB effective working set.

A few heuristics to pick the primary reserve SKU: (we'll convert to a checklist)
1) If >30% of tokens are long-context (>=8k) and you need <10% tail-latency degradation: H100 preferred.
2) If long-context is intermittent and memory footprint per request <40GB: A100 acceptable.
3) If >70% traffic is <512 tokens and P95<300ms is critical: L4 pool for chat, with A100/H100 fallback for heavy document ops.

Proposed immediate action items:
- We will produce a 3-sku reserve proposal: base reserved pool (A100), a long-context reserve cluster (H100) sized for 40% long-context concurrency, and an autoscale L4 burst pool for chat spikes.
- Ask Integrata to run a 48-hour validation spike (we can help run a controlled load test) and share token distribution traces + p95/p99 latency by model and sequence length.

Telemetry checklist (short):
- Token sequence length histogram (per request)
- Per-model KV cache hit ratio and reuse distribution
- Per-request memory working set & GPU memory pressure events
- Tail latency (p95/p99) breakdown by SKU and sequence bucket
- Token/sec per GPU and effective tokens per dollar during the spike

I attached a concise SKU decision checklist and a blank MAP (mutual action plan) — see attached.

If that looks good I'll draft the reserved vs burst numbers and a pricing sketch to match your procurement cadence.

Best,

Thanks Erin & Karthik — quick operational checklist and a lightweight scorecard we use internally to pick a primary SKU for a Dedicated commit. Posting here so procurement has visibility when they scope the commitment.

"SKU Decision Scorecard" (one-line rules, score out of 100):
- Long-context exposure (0-40 points): weight by % of total tokens that are >8k. >30% = 40pts, 15-30%=25pts, <15%=5pts.
- Memory working set per concurrent request (0-25 points): >48GB=25pts, 32-48GB=15pts, <32GB=5pts.
- Latency sensitivity (0-20 points): P95 target <300ms = 0 for H100/A100 (they add latency for long context), L4 favored gives 20pts.
- Cost sensitivity / tokens-per-dollar (0-15 points): if target tokens/$ is tight, L4 or quantized A100 wins.

Interpretation: score >=60 => pick H100 pool as primary reserved (long-context heavy). Score 35-59 => A100 primary with H100 for long ops. Score <35 => A set of L4 clusters for chat with on-demand A100 fallback.

Sizing note (rough numbers to validate in spike):
- If you plan 40% long-context at 120 QPS peak: assume 8 concurrent long-context requests per GPU on H100 (typical with KV caching and batching) — we will produce a capacity table in the proposal.
- Keep a 15-20% reserved buffer for GC/pinning and concurrency variance.

Commercial & contracting liaisons: Dev (cc'd) will slot the pricing sketch & term variants (monthly reserved vs yearly commit). For procurement: we can provide a PoC quote for a 30-day validation period with reduced financial commitment.

-Lauren
Lauren Bishop
